'''Bilal Coulibaly''' ({{IPAc-en|b|i|ˈ|l|ɑː|l|_|ˌ|k|uː|l|ɪ|ˈ|b|ɑː|l|i}} {{respell|bee|LAHL|_|KOO|lih|BAH|lee}}; {{IPA|fr|bilal kulibali|lang}}; born 26 July 2004) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played for the [[Metropolitans 92]] of [[LNB Pro A]] prior to being selected seventh overall by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the [[2023 NBA draft]]. Coulibaly has also played for the [[France men's national basketball team|French national team]], winning silver at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Summer Olympics]].

==Early life==
Coulibaly was born on 26 July 2004 in [[Saint-Cloud, France]], a [[Communes of France|commune]] of Paris. He grew up in nearby [[Courbevoie]] and began playing basketball for Courbevoie Sport Basket at age eight. He began playing for the youth team of [[Levallois Sporting Club Basket]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/qui-est-bilal-coulibaly-lautre-pepite-des-metropolitans-92/ |title=Qui est Bilal Coulibaly, l'autre pépite des Metropolitans 92? |website=bebasket.fr |date=19 January 2023 |access-date=25 April 2023 |language=fr}}</ref> He is of [[Mali]]an descent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mabel |first=Winnie |date=23 June 2023 |title=8 players with African roots make it into NBA 2023 draft list |url=https://nairobinews.nation.africa/8-players-with-african-roots-make-it-into-nba-2023-draft-list/ |access-date=24 June 2023 |website=Nairobi News}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Metropolitans 92 (2021–2023)===
[[File:Bilal Coulibaly.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Coulibaly with [[Metropolitans 92]] in 2023]]
Coulibaly began playing professionally for [[Metropolitans 92]] in LNB Espoirs, the French under-21 league, in 2021. He began the 2022–23 season playing for the Metropolitans 92 under-21 team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/basket/le-mans/basket-elite-valentin-chery-et-bilal-coulibaly-etaient-en-mission-defensive-pendant-mets-92-msb-0089776a-ce45-11ed-8922-c50b96804298 |title=Basket. Élite : Valentin Chery et Bilal Coulibaly étaient en mission défensive pendant Mets 92 - MSB |work=[[Ouest-France]] |date=29 March 2023 |access-date=30 March 2023 |language=fr}}</ref> He was promoted to the senior team after averaging 21.9 points, 2.6 steals, and 1.2 blocks per game in the LNB Espoirs competition. He played alongside future NBA Rookie of the Year [[Victor Wembanyama]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/international-spotlight-the-rise-of-bilal-coulibaly |title=International Spotlight: The Rise of Bilal Coulibaly |first=Ignacio |last=Rissotto |website=[[SI.com]] |date=19 February 2023 |access-date=30 March 2023}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2023–present)===
====2023–2024: Rookie Year====
The [[Indiana Pacers]] selected Coulibaly with the seventh overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]] and traded his rights to the [[Washington Wizards]] for two future second-round picks and the draft rights to [[Jarace Walker]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/36244098 |title=Bilal Coulibaly joins teammate Victor Wembanyama in NBA draft |first=Jonathan |last=Givony |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=20 April 2023 |access-date=21 April 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Ava |last=Wallace |title=Wizards, with eye on long-term future, take French project Bilal Coulibaly |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2023/06/22/bilal-coulibaly-wizards-draft/ |agency=The Washington Post |date=23 June 2023 |access-date=23 June 2023}}</ref> On 2 July 2023, he signed with the Wizards.<ref>{{cite tweet |author=Washington Wizards |title=pen to paper ✍️ @Bilaal_6 signed his contract this morning. |number=1675565091964559360 |user=WashWizards |date=2 July 2023 |access-date=16 September 2023}}</ref> He joined Washington during the [[2023 NBA Summer League]] and ended the four games averaging 12.3 points per game and 4.8 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bilal Coulibaly | Washington Wizards |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1641731/bilal-coulibaly/ |access-date=31 January 2024 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref> Coulibaly made his NBA debut in the Wizards' season opener on 25 October, and recorded three points, four rebounds, three assists, and three blocks in 23 minutes played in a 143–120 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/wizards-bilal-coulibaly-three-points-in-pro-debut/ |title=Wizards' Bilal Coulibaly: Three points in pro debut |website=[[CBS Sports]] |agency=[[RotoWire]] |date=26 October 2023 |access-date=26 October 2023}}</ref> Shortly after, on 30 October, in a game against the [[Boston Celtics]], Coulibaly would become the youngest player in Wizards franchise history to start a game at just 19 years and 96 days.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bilal Coulibaly Selected as Rising Star |url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/bilal-coulibaly-selected-as-rising-star |access-date=31 January 2024 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref> Coulibaly recorded his first double-double with Washington in a 8 December game against the [[Brooklyn Nets]], where he scored 11 points and grabbed 10 rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Waller |first=Candi |date=9 December 2023 |title=Washington Wizards Rookie Bilal Coulibaly Records First Career Double Double |url=https://www.si.com/nba/wizards/news/wizards-rookie-bilal-coulibaly-records-first-career-double-double |access-date=31 January 2024 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref>

On 18 March 2024, the Wizards announced that Coulibaly would miss the remainder of the 2023–24 season with a right wrist fracture that he suffered in a game against the [[Chicago Bulls]]. In his rookie season, Coulibaly played in 63 games (starting 15) and averaged 8.4 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 1.7 assists.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 March 2024 |title=Wizards rookie Bilal Coulibaly (wrist) to miss rest of season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39761760/wizards-rookie-bilal-coulibaly-wrist-miss-rest-season |access-date=18 March 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2024–2025====
Coulibaly started 59 contests for the Wizards during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 12.3 points, five rebounds, and 3.4 assists. In March 2025, he suffered a right hamstring strain that forced him to miss the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Wizards guard Bilal Coulibaly is out 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44236791/wizards-guard-bilal-coulibaly-4-6-weeks-hamstring-injury|access-date=28 April 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

====2025–2026====
On 12 September 2025, it was announced that Coulibaly had undergone surgery to repair a torn ligament in his right thumb.<ref>{{cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=2025-09-12 |title=Wizards G Coulibaly has thumb surgery in NYC |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46234894/sources-wizards-coulibaly-thumb-surgery-ligament-tear |access-date=2025-12-06 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==National team career==
Coulibaly played for the [[France men's national under-19 basketball team|France national under-18 team]] in the [[2022 FIBA U18 European Championship]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/insider/insider/story/_/id/34396935 |title=The top 11 NBA prospects at the FIBA U18 European Championship |first=Jonathan |last=Givony |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=15 August 2022 |access-date=25 April 2023}}</ref> He averaged 7.7 points, 3.9 rebounds, and one assist over seven games as France finished in fifth place.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2023/04/20/metropolitans-92-bilal-coulibaly-2023-nba-mock-draft/ |title=International prospect Bilal Coulibaly declares for 2023 NBA draft |first=Cody |last=Taylor |website=The Rookie Wire |publisher=[[USA Today]] |date=20 April 2023 |access-date=25 April 2023}}</ref> Coulibaly played with the [[France men's national basketball team|national team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Summer Olympics]], earning a silver medal after losing to the [[2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team|United States]] in the finals.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mullin |first1=Eric |title=A look at the NBA players competing in the Olympics |url=https://www.nbclosangeles.com/paris-2024-summer-olympics/nba-players-2024-olympics-mens-basketball-teams-paris/3456221/ |website=NBC Los Angeles |date=10 July 2024 |access-date=20 July 2024}}</ref>
